questions.q: What are the two YAML blocks this lesson uses to turn a mart into a queryable metric?
options: A semantic_models block describing the table, then a metrics block built on top of it
A single models: block with no other configuration
A snapshot block and a seed block
Only a metrics block — semantic models are not required
questions.explain: MetricFlow needs a semantic_models entry describing entities/dimensions/measures first, then a metrics entry built on top of a measure.

questions.q: Inside a semantic model, what is a 'measure'?
options: A column you'd aggregate — the raw input a metric is built from
A key column used to join to another table
A column you'd only ever group or filter by, never aggregate
The name of the BI tool connecting to the metric
questions.explain: Measures are aggregatable columns (like order_total, summed) — the raw input metrics like revenue get built from.

questions.q: In the `revenue` metric example, where does the 'exclude cancelled orders' rule live?
options: Inside the metric's own filter definition, in version-controlled YAML
In three different analysts' personal spreadsheets
Nowhere — it must be re-applied manually every time someone queries revenue
Only inside the BI tool's own private calculation
questions.explain: The filter is part of the metric's definition itself, so every consuming tool automatically gets the same exclusion — no one has to remember to re-apply it.

questions.q: What does a `type: simple` metric wrap?
options: Exactly one measure, with an optional filter
An entire semantic layer with no measures at all
Every metric in the whole project at once
A raw SQL query with no relation to any measure
questions.explain: A simple metric is the most basic type: one measure, plus an optional filter — more complex metric types build on top of this.

questions.q: Once `revenue` is defined, how does a connected BI tool get that number, according to this lesson?
options: It queries the metric by name (e.g. through the Query Builder), without re-deriving the SQL or the filter itself
It must still write its own custom SQL to replicate the filter
It has to copy the YAML file directly into the BI tool
Metrics cannot be queried by external tools at all
questions.explain: Any connected tool asks the semantic layer for the metric by name — the Query Builder shows Select Metrics: revenue, with no SQL and no re-derived filter logic.
